test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said to me, “I shall come to meet you tomorrow.”

options.text: She asked me that could she come to meet me the next day.
She tells me that she could come to meet me tomorrow.
She told me that she would come to meet me the next day.
She told me that she will come to meet me tomorrow.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
 
__ 
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She told me that she would come to meet me the next day. 
 
• **Key Conversions:** 
 
 
• **"I shall come to meet you tomorrow" becomes "she would come to meet me the next day"** 
 
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to match the subject of the reporting verb. 
 
• Shall is changed to would to match the future tense in indirect speech. 
 
• Time expression "tomorrow" is changed to "the next day". 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:** 
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks in the original sentence. 
 
• Indirect speech does not use quotation marks and follows a declarative format. 
 
 
 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *She told me that she would come to meet me the next day.* 
 
 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
 
• **Option 1:** "She asked me that could she come to meet me the next day." 
 
 
• Incorrect structure for indirect speech. The original sentence is a statement, not a question. 
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She tells me that she could come to meet me tomorrow." 
 
 
• Incorrect tense. "Tells" should be in the past tense as "told" to match the reporting verb. 
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She told me that she will come to meet me tomorrow." 
 
 
• Incorrect future tense. "Will" should be changed to "would" in indirect speech.
